artifact_text:
### Observations

1. Pod `billing-api-5bb97fbdc4-4szcr` logs repeat `WARN db connection reset by peer, retrying (pool acquire ...)` alongside memory pressure warnings.
2. In `ack-system`, `DBProxy/billing-db-proxy` sets `idleClientTimeout: 600` (applied in CI-2452), whereas `Deployment/billing-api` configures `DB_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: "900"`.
3. Prometheus metrics show `db_connection_wait_seconds{service="billing-api"}` rising above 2.2 seconds concurrently with heap growth up to 360 MB.

### Ruled-out leads

1. Application memory leak was ruled out because heap growth is a side effect of stalled requests during pool exhaustion (RB-014, INC-2024-0312).
2. Load balancer keep-alive mismatch was ruled out because CI-2455 already aligned the ALB and HTTP keep-alive timeouts to 120s and 125s.

### Root cause

The RDS DBProxy `idleClientTimeout` (600s) is shorter than the `billing-api` connection pool recycling timeout (900s), causing silent connection drops and pool exhaustion.

### Recommended action

The infrastructure team must remove or increase `idleClientTimeout` on `DBProxy/billing-db-proxy` in `ack-system` above 900s to restore AWS default recycling.
